subject: Repack options and impact: compact -> throughput with feature bundling
messages:
From: Patrick O'Connor <patrick@clearline.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearLine Procurement <procurement@clearline.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Repack options and impact: compact -> throughput with feature bundling

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating a move from our current Compact plan to a Throughput-oriented package for two reasons: 1) higher concurrent request throughput for chat + embeddings, and 2) a bundled set of features (KV caching and prefix cache preserver) we'd like to enable across three high-volume routes.

Before we lock anything in, procurement asked me to confirm a few operational and commercial points so we can decide whether to: upgrade mid-term, do a phased roll, or request a credit/proration for unused Compact credits. Can you confirm:

- If we upgrade mid-contract, how does proration work for the remaining billing term? Any manual credits or automatic true-up?
- Can individual routes be pinned to the old model/plan while others migrate (we have two customer-facing routes that must remain low-latency)?
- Are feature bundles transferrable between plans (e.g., move KV caching entitlement from Compact seats to Throughput pool)?
- Any restrictions on quantized model variants when using dedicated Throughput pools?

Also, if you can share a simple repack matrix (features vs. plans + expected cost delta) that would help our procurement/engineering review.

CC'ing procurement for visibility. Happy to do a 30-45m workshop next week to walk through options.

Cheers,
Patrick
Patrick O'Connor

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repack options and impact: compact -> throughput with feature bundling

Patrick — thanks for the clear list. I put together three pragmatic paths depending on how aggressive you want the change to be. High level: phased, swap-with-credit, or immediate throughput swap.

Summary of options (short):
- Option A — Phased roll (recommended): Keep customer-facing routes on Compact with a route-level pin while we move internal/analytics routes to Throughput. No SLA impact on pinned routes. Minimal proration (we bill new throughput consumption; unused Compact credits roll into a 30-day deferred credit).
- Option B — Swap-with-credit: Convert to Throughput now; we calculate the unused Compact credit and apply it against the first Throughput invoice. Standard proration formula applies (daily pro-rata based on committed token/seat value), and procurement can request an upfront manual credit if needed.
- Option C — Immediate swap (fastest): We switch everything to Throughput; you lose route pins, but we provide a 2-week grace window with automatic fallback to previous model variants if latency regressions surface. Proration is as Option B.

Notes on feature bundling and transfer: feature entitlements (KV cache, prefix cache preserver, per-route tracing hooks) are transferable to Throughput pools but entitlement movement requires an amendment and may change the billing SKU. For seat-to-throughput crediting we typically produce a one-line amendment that procurement signs; I've attached a draft amendment and a one-tab repack matrix showing estimated cost deltas.

Technical caveats (Ben added a couple):
- Quantized variants: 8-bit/4-bit usable in Throughput but performance differs by model type; some larger models may show higher latency when aggressively quantized under low-latency SLOs. Ben's notes attached.
- Dedicated pools: If you add dedicated GPUs for Throughput, we can pin model kernels to hardware, which reduces variance but raises committed cost.

Attachments: proposed-repack-matrix.xlsx (pricing delta table), amendment-draft.pdf (one-line amendment template), quantization-impact-notes.txt

Next steps: if this looks reasonable, can we schedule a 45m workshop Thurs (7/15) or Fri (7/16)? I'll have Ben and Lauren join to walk technical and billing impacts.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Repack options and impact: compact -> throughput with feature bundling

Adding a few technical specifics so procurement/eng can see trade-offs before the workshop:

- Route-level pinning: We can pin routes at the inference gateway level. That preserves TTLs/KV caches for pinned routes. There is a small additional operational cost (per-route cache reservation) but no performance downside.
- Quantization: For the family of models you're using (gpt-family-large-v1), 8-bit quantization is generally safe for throughput workloads; 4-bit can shave cost but increases the chance of slight decoding artifacts on long prompts. If low-latency SLOs are crucial for customer-facing routes, keep those on 8-bit or full fp16 on dedicated GPUs.
- Feature bundling: KV caching entitlements are primarily a runtime config change, but if you're moving from Compact seats that had caching built-in to a shared Throughput pool we need to migrate your prefix cache allocations; that's a one-time migration operation and a short maintenance window (<15 min) if you accept cached warming.

I attached a short note with benchmarks we ran last quarter comparing latencies for Compact vs Throughput under pinned vs unpinned scenarios. Happy to present numbers on Thurs.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: quantization-impact-notes.txt
